content.content:
Apply to the decision's recorded inline text, read against the four prerequisites. The decision passes only if all six criteria hold; fail on any missing element or on any contradiction, naming the element and, where it applies, the prerequisite.
1. One root, held and lent. The text opens the store on one root and keeps it the only root the store holds: no second root, no root discovery of its own, no retry or re-open on another root. Fail on any clause letting the store choose, probe for, or fall back to a root after it is opened (ppwnzwwy: the store holds one repo root, lends it, and has no reach of its own).
2. No interface re-decides the root. Every graph-file kind the text opens (store read, store write, markers, exclude, journal) is opened on the store's root; none resolves a root from the invocation, the caller, or any origin of its own. Fail on a clause in which any file kind's root is chosen anywhere but at the store (xquwmsts).
3. Root identity is a place, not a label. The trunk root is the working copy root that contains the repository's state directory, fixed by where the state directory sits and not by a change id, a workspace name, or whatever change the working copy has checked out; a draft workspace root — under the per-user root, outside the repository, at the directory its handle names — is not that place and cannot serve as the store root. Fail if the text names the trunk by anything other than place, or treats a root outside the repository as a candidate store root (xqzstoyo, uqqswnsy).
4. The anchor stays apart. The invocation's jj commands keep running against the invocation workspace root, so rooting the store at the trunk does not move the working copy a draft invocation edits. Fail if the text roots both the store and the jj runner on one root, which would put a draft invocation's jj edits in the trunk working copy (xqzstoyo: a draft workspace is another working copy of the tree, outside the repository).
5. Refusal, never fallback. When the trunk root cannot be resolved from the invocation workspace, the text admits only a refusal that names the cause: it permits nothing opened on the invocation workspace root, no state directory created to manufacture a root, no probe for another root, and no continued run with a root-less store. Fail on any clause admitting one of these, and name it (ppwnzwwy: one root and no reach; xquwmsts: no interface re-decides the root; xqzstoyo: a state directory is a directory of the repository's own working copy; uqqswnsy: no draft workspace reads or writes the marker stack).
6. Non-contradiction. No element of the text contradicts a prerequisite: in particular, no element places the marker stack, the exclude file, the journal or the node documents under a working copy that does not hold the state directory, and no element lets a draft workspace read or write the marker stack. Fail on the contradicting element, naming the prerequisite.
content.rationale: Both endpoints are prose commitments, so the edge takes a non-runnable gate form. The dependent's content is text (natural layer), and of the four prerequisites three carry inline prose (natural) while ppwnzwwy's content is prose in a node whose ref is source (code layer); with a natural child the cells are natural-to-natural for three edges and code-to-natural for the fourth, whose row is the matrix default — the gate form plus a flag that the ppwnzwwy cell (code parent, natural child) has no matrix entry yet. A prose child is checked for non-violation and never for behavior, so the recorded form is review-criteria with inline criteria applied by a reviewer to the dependent's text: what this layer can settle is whether the text buys the root once, never re-decides it below the store, names the trunk by place, keeps the invocation anchor apart, and refuses rather than falls back. Each criterion is traced to the prerequisite that states it and names no element of a future implementation, so a rewrite of the decision that still decides the same thing leaves the criteria intact.
